title: Bài sưu tầm 329 - Passage 3: Measuring Progress Beyond GDP: Why Economic Statistics Miss Everyday Life
passageHtml:
READING PASSAGE 329

Measuring Progress Beyond GDP: Why Economic Statistics Miss Everyday Life

Paragraph 1. Every quarter, financial headlines celebrate or mourn tiny movements in Gross Domestic Product (GDP). Introduced during the Great Depression of the 1930s to help governments track industrial output and war-readiness, GDP simply adds up the monetary value of goods and services bought and sold within a country's borders. Ironically, its chief architect, American economist Simon Kuznets, warned the US Congress in 1934 that the welfare of a nation could scarcely be inferred from a measurement of national income.

Paragraph 2. Kuznets' warning highlights glaring blind spots in how GDP counts value. Because it tracks only paid market transactions, vast amounts of essential social work remain completely invisible. Preparing family meals, caring for elderly relatives, or volunteering at local schools contribute enormously to community stability, yet register as zero in national accounts. Conversely, when a household hires a private caregiver or eats every meal at a restaurant, GDP rises—even though the actual care or nutrition provided may be unchanged.

Paragraph 3. Even more troubling is GDP’s indifference to environmental destruction and social costs. If a timber company clears an ancient forest, the sale of logs boosts economic growth immediately, while the loss of clean water, soil stability, and future timber reserves is never subtracted. Similarly, an oil spill or a surge in traffic accidents generates spending on cleanup crews, hospital bills, and vehicle repairs—all of which technically count as economic 'gains.'

Paragraph 4. In response, economists and international bodies have proposed broader indicators—such as the Genuine Progress Indicator (GPI) and New Zealand’s Wellbeing Budget—that factor in unpaid labour, income distribution, and ecological health. Yet replacing GDP has proven politically difficult. GDP offers politicians a single, familiar number that is quick to calculate and easy to compare across nations, whereas multi-dimensional indices force governments to confront uncomfortable trade-offs between short-term industrial output and long-term sustainability.

groups.title: Questions 36–39
groups.instructions: Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer in Reading Passage 329? In boxes 36–39 on your answer sheet, write YES, NO or NOT GIVEN.

groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D. Write the correct letter in box 40 on your answer sheet.

q27.text: Why does the writer mention Simon Kuznets’s 1934 address to the US Congress?
options: A. to show that GDP was originally intended to measure personal happiness
B. to emphasize that even GDP's creator recognized its limits as a measure of wellbeing
C. to argue that the Great Depression prevented accurate economic recording
D. to prove that wartime industrial output was lower than expected

steps: Đoạn 1: Chính cha đẻ GDP (Kuznets) đã cảnh báo rằng phúc lợi quốc gia khó có thể suy ra từ thước đo thu nhập quốc dân.
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q28.text: The example of hiring a private caregiver illustrates how GDP
options: A. underestimates the high cost of professional healthcare services.
B. treats identical activities differently depending on whether money changes hands.
C. discourages families from supporting elderly relatives at home.
D. excludes restaurant spending from official national accounts.

steps: Đoạn 2: Người nhà tự chăm thì GDP = 0, thuê người chăm thì GDP tăng dù chất lượng chăm sóc không đổi (phụ thuộc việc có trả tiền hay không).
Kết luận: Chọn B.

q29.text: What flaw in GDP does the third paragraph expose through the examples of logging and oil spills?
options: A. It fails to count jobs created in the forestry sector.
B. It records repair and extraction revenues without deducting damage.
C. It exaggerates the long-term financial profits of car manufacturers.
D. It ignores the immediate cost of emergency hospital treatment.

steps: Đoạn 3: Tiền bán gỗ và chi phí dọn dẹp/sửa chữa đều cộng vào tăng trưởng, còn tổn thất tài nguyên thiên nhiên không bao giờ bị trừ đi.
Kết luận: Chọn B.
Đoạn 2: Preparing family meals, caring for elderly relatives ↔ domestic (E) labour.
Đoạn 3: technically count as economic 'gains' ↔ artificially inflated (H).
Đoạn 3: an oil spill or a surge in traffic accidents ↔ disasters (F).
Đoạn 3: the loss of clean water, soil stability, and future timber reserves ↔ depletion (C).
Đoạn 4: a single, familiar number that is quick to calculate and easy to compare ↔ straightforward (B) benchmark.
Đoạn 4: uncomfortable trade-offs ↔ policy compromises (D).

q36.text: Unpaid school volunteering is included in standard GDP calculations if it benefits local families.

steps: Đoạn 2: "volunteering at local schools... register as zero in national accounts."
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q37.text: New Zealand was the first country in the world to formally replace GDP with a Wellbeing Budget.

steps: Đoạn 4: Bài có nhắc Ngân sách Phúc lợi của New Zealand, nhưng không nói đây là nước đầu tiên hay đã chính thức thay thế hoàn toàn GDP.
Kết luận: Chọn NOT GIVEN.

q38.text: Complex wellbeing indices are generally harder to reduce to a single headline figure than GDP.

steps: Đoạn 4: GDP cho ra một con số duy nhất dễ tính/so sánh, trong khi các chỉ số đa chiều buộc chính phủ đối diện nhiều đánh đổi phức tạp.
Kết luận: Chọn YES.

q39.text: Rising GDP figures always reflect an improvement in a population's overall quality of life.

steps: Đoạn 1 & 3: Sự cố tràn dầu, tai nạn giao thông hay tàn phá rừng đều làm tăng GDP nhưng không cải thiện chất lượng sống.
Kết luận: Chọn NO.

q40.text: Which subtitle would be most suitable for Reading Passage 329?
options: A. How Simon Kuznets designed the world's most accurate economic tool
B. Why unpaid domestic labour is disappearing in modern economies
C. What national growth figures reveal—and conceal—about human welfare
D. The complete failure of international environmental agreements

steps: Chủ đề xuyên suốt bài: Chỉ số tăng trưởng GDP đo được gì và che khuất những gì về phúc lợi con người.
Kết luận: Chọn C.
